chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

Regarding the washer and the goldsmith: if something is stolen from them, and they do not bring clear proof concerning a manifest matter that it was indeed stolen, then for any amount, small or great, they are liable. But if they do so, then nothing is upon them. And if he does not establish proof and claims that what was alleged has gone, then he is liable for it if he has no proof for his statement.

key_terms.الصُّوَّاغِ: the goldsmith; a craftsman entrusted with valuables for work
key_terms.الْغُسَّالِ: the washer; a person entrusted with garments or goods for washing
key_terms.بِبَيِّنَةٍ: with clear proof or legal evidence
key_terms.ضَمِنَهُ: he is liable for it and must compensate for it
key_terms.قَوْلِهِ: his claim or statement in the dispute

ai.seo_question: When is a washer or goldsmith liable for property claimed to have been stolen or lost?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal ruling concerning entrusted property in the hands of workers such as a washer or a goldsmith. If they claim that the property was stolen or lost, they must establish that claim by clear evidence; otherwise, they are financially liable for what was entrusted to them.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "Regarding the washer (ghassal) and the goldsmith (sawwagh), if something is stolen from them and they do not provide clear evidence proving that it was stolen, whether it is little or much, then they are liable. However, if they establish proof with clear evidence, then they are not liable. But if they fail to present evidence and merely claim that the item was lost, they are responsible for compensating it unless they provide proof to support their claim."
